proposals.impact: recover 9 sessions stuck at intro_load before q1
proposals.observation: In the last 48 hours, 10 sessions hit the quiz. 9 of those sessions stopped at intro_load. Only 1 reached q1_shown. Zero completions. The bottleneck is not drop-off mid-quiz. Nobody is leaving mid-quiz. They are not clicking into q1 at all. The intro screen is the entire problem.
proposals.proposal: The intro CTA is almost certainly too vague, too slow to load a next action, or buried below the fold on mobile. Pull the current intro button text and any surrounding copy. The replacement needs to tell the visitor in plain, specific language what happens when they click, and why it is worth 3 minutes of their life right now. Use Joel's real voice: the person landing here earns well, knows something is off, and is quietly hoping this is not just another quiz. Speak to that. One sentence of grounding, one concrete description of what the quiz produces, one button. No scroll required on 375px viewport.

proposals.new_text:
You earn well. The numbers should feel steadier than they do.

This is a 3-minute quiz built around the Klontz Money Script research. It tells you which money belief pattern is quietly running your financial decisions, with a short written explanation sent straight to your inbox.

Start the quiz

Joel Nwosu, MSc Behavioural Economics | Qualified Financial Planner. No sales pitch at the end.

proposals.impact: lift 37.5% open rate closer to Money Vigilance benchmark
proposals.observation: The Money Worship automation has a 37.5% open rate across 16 sends. Money Vigilance sits at 66.67% on 12 sends. Money Avoidance is at 52.63% on 19 sends. Money Worship is the weakest by a wide margin. The most likely cause is the subject line of email 1, which is where open rates are set. Given that Money Worship subscribers have just been told they tie self-worth to income, the subject line needs to meet them in that specific tension, not in a generic "here's your result" frame.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the subject line of money-worship email 1 only. Do not touch the email body. The new subject line should name the specific internal experience of someone who links status to net worth, earns more than their friends, and still feels like it is never quite enough. No motivational framing. No question marks designed to create curiosity gaps. A sentence that sounds like Joel recognises something the subscriber has not said aloud yet.
proposals.current_text: subject: Your Money Worship result is inside
proposals.new_text: subject: When earning more didn't make it feel like enough

proposals.impact: unblock automated content publishing (1 post queued, workflow failing since 07:58)
proposals.observation: The Daily Blog Post workflow has been failing since 07:58 this morning. There is 1 post queued. The Funnel-Hack Digest workflow also failed at 12:55. Two separate workflow failures in the same day suggests either a shared dependency (an API key, a Node version, a broken import) or a runner environment change on GitHub's side. With only 1 post in the queue, a second day of failure means the queue empties and content publishing stops entirely.
proposals.proposal: Open the Daily Blog Post workflow file and check three things in order: the Node version pinned in the workflow against what the repo's package.json expects, any API key environment variable references (compare the variable names in the YML against the names set in GitHub Secrets), and whether the error log from the 07:58 run contains the same root message as the Funnel-Hack Digest failure at 12:55. If they share the same error, fix the shared cause first. The minimal change here is correcting whichever single line is mismatched. Do not restructure the workflow. Do not upgrade dependencies. One-line fix, re-run, confirm green before end of day so the queued post publishes tonight.
